https://www.politico.eu/article/20-count.text: NEW YORK — Several European countries were among a group of 22 nations that adopted a declaration Monday saying that artificial intelligence “must remain under human direction, oversight and control” and suggesting to create a global supervisory regime. The declaration , adopted on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly this week, acknowledged AI’s “potential to improve lives, advance science and strengthen our economies” but warned that “the rapid development of frontier AI models poses serious risks to safety and security if not appropriately managed.” The push comes ahead of the meeting of U.S. President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping, the leaders of the world’s leading AI-developing nations, in Washington Thursday. Advertisement Advertisement Neither the U.S. nor China are part of the new declaration. But Finnish President Alexander Stubb, one of the main organizers of the document, told POLITICO that he hopes to create “momentum” and get more actors on board: “I think it will be in the interest of both China and the United States to have some kind of guardrails. And our message here is that we need human intervention, so humans need to be in charge,” he said in an interview. Referring to the recent cyberattack by rogue AI agents on the Hugging Face platform , the declaration urges to “address these risks” by obliging AI companies “to develop transparent safety protocols, including mandatory pre-deployment testing and independent evaluation, with qualified evaluators granted sufficient access to assess risks.” Yet the document falls short of calling for slowing down or pausing AI development, with organizers saying they want to focus on managing risks instead. Alexander Stubb, one of the main organizers of the document, told POLITICO that he hopes to create “momentum” and get more actors on board: “I think it will be in the interest of both China and the United States to have some kind of guardrails. | Alessandro Rampazzo/ AFP via Getty Images To do that, countries should “further develop and coordinate common standards” and strengthen transparency, “including shared reporting of serious safety incidents.” Moreover, UN member countries should “build on existing international mechanisms and explore creating an international institution” to oversee AI. Stubb, who spoke to POLITICO at Finland’s consular office in New York, said that “our preference personally” would be to create a new institution similar to the International Atomic Energy Agency “within the U.N. framework.” Yet he added, with a nod to Trump’s skepticism of the United Nations, “we have to leave it open-ended so that people don’t reject it just because it would be within the U.N. framework.” Norway’s Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre, who initiated the declaration together with Stubb and who joined the interview via video, said that, “we would be very encouraged to see both G7 and the upcoming G20 presidency of the United Kingdom take on this ... The U.N. is big, but the G7, G20 is a bit more focused.” Advertisement Advertisement However, the U.K. has not signed up to the declaration yet. Among the big European countries, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz supports the initiative, while signatures from France, Italy and Poland are notably absent. Stubb added that neither he nor Støre were “doomsdayers” about artificial intelligence but named three reasons why the lack of effective oversight is threatening: AI-created bioweapons, cyberattacks by AI agents and killer robots using AI for lethal attacks. Stubb stressed that the upside of AI can be “much higher” — if the tech is used correctly — ranging from “the eradication of diseases, productivity, information and many other things.”

https://www.euronews.com/2026/10/26/zele.text: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said on Monday that Kyiv had been waiting for almost a month for US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth to sign off on much coveted Patriot interceptor missiles.In an update on weapons supplies shared on social media, Zelenskyy said Ukraine had been awaiting approval to receive missiles for both the Patriot and NASAMS systems."We are working on several tracks – with the United States, Europe, and other partners that have stocks of PAC-2 and PAC-3 missiles," he wrote."In particular, we have been waiting for nearly a month for Mr. Hegseth to sign off on missiles for Patriots and NASAMS," Zelenskyy continued, adding that he had instructed his team to raise the issue with Washington once again."Conversations with other countries are also ongoing," he said.Kyiv has repeatedly pressed the need for more interceptors to be delivered to its forces as Ukraine continues to defend against deadly Russian missile attacks and jet-powered drone strikes.On Sunday, Zelenskyy said Russian forces had fired 48 missiles - including ballistic missiles - at Ukraine over the past week, as well as around 1,600 guided aerial bombs and close to 2,300 attack drones."Unfortunately, almost every day, these brutal strikes leave people killed and injured," he wrote on X. "We need to unblock the deliveries of Patriot interceptors already approved by European countries."The Patriot missile platform is one of the world's most advanced air defence systems and can be used to defend against a variety of threats, including aircraft and ballistic missiles.Ukraine receives the majority of its Patriot missiles through NATO’s Prioritised Ukraine Requirements List (PURL) initiative, which facilitates the purchase of military equipment and munitions from the US by allies and partners.As of June 2026, allies had committed to funding more than $6 billion of defence equipment for Ukraine through the scheme, per NATO.Munitions stockpiles under strainGlobal munitions stocks have come under significant pressure in recent months amid the US' war in Iran.A report from the US Department of Defence's inspector general, published in September, said American forces had fired $22.3 billion worth of munitions from the start of Operation Epic Fury in late February to the end of June.Yurii Ihnat, a colonel in the Ukrainian military, said in an interview published on Monday that the number of Patriot missiles used in the Middle East could have supported several years of combat operations in Ukraine.It is unclear how many of the missiles Ukraine is waiting for Hegseth to sign off on, although Ukrainian media reports suggest that it is a sizeable figure.

https://www.digi24.ro/stiri/externe/trim.text: Preşedintele ucrainean Volodimir Zelenski a afirmat că negociatorii americani au ridicat problema unei posibile retrageri a Ucrainei din regiunea estică Donbas, în schimbul aderării la NATO, în urma celei mai recente runde de discuţii de pace cu Rusia, desfăşurate la Abu Dhabi, relatează sâmbătă Reuters. Zelenski şi-a reiterat poziţia, subliniind că Kievul nu este dispus să se retragă de pe teritoriul său. El a precizat că, în cazul în care Ucraina ar primi un pachet cuprinzător de securitate - care să includă garanţii de securitate, o armată ucraineană puternică şi bine finanţată, precum şi fonduri pentru reconstrucţie -, ar supune această chestiune unui referendum. „Americanii au ridicat o problemă: Ce-ar fi dacă Ucraina ar adera la NATO? S-ar retrage Ucraina din Donbas? A fost prima dată când s-a pus această chestiune”, le-a spus Zelenski jurnaliştilor, potrivit unor declaraţii date publicităţii sâmbătă de biroul său. „De aceea consider că subiectul NATO a revenit pe agendă. Dar aţi auzit şi semnalele transmise de (preşedintele rus Vladimir) Putin; este o discuţie extrem de dificilă”, a adăugat el. Consilierul Kremlinului, Iuri Ușakov, a declarat că Vladimir Putin va continua discuțiile cu Donald Trump privind războiul din Ucraina în cadrul unei întâlniri programate săptămâna viitoare, în China. Ușakov a afirmat că Moscova este pregătită să discute cu Washingtonul despre viitorul securității europene. „Rusia este pregătită să înceapă imediat discuții, împreună cu Statele Unite, cu privire la propunerile referitoare la securitatea europeană”, a spus oficialul rus. „Actualul sistem de securitate european nu funcționează și sperăm că europenii vor sprijini o nouă arhitectură a securității indivizibile, pe care Rusia și Statele Unite sunt pregătite să o stabilească~, a adăugat acesta. Solicitările Moscovei privind un rol mai important în stabilirea aranjamentelor de securitate ale Europei nu sunt noi. La începutul anului 2021, Rusia a transmis Statelor Unite și NATO o serie de propuneri care vizau limitarea extinderii Alianței și a prezenței sale militare în apropierea granițelor ruse. Potrivit lui Zelenski, UE şi NATO reprezintă singura „securitate reală” pentru Europa şi că încercarea Kremlinului de a modifica arhitectura de securitate a continentului este „periculoasă” şi ar putea duce la noi războaie. „Este periculos, deoarece, în opinia mea, tocmai astfel de lucruri duc la războaie sau la escaladări”, a declarat președintele ucrainean. El a adăugat că „singura securitate reală pentru Europa este reprezentată de UE şi NATO”. „Asta e tot. Nu există o altă securitate pentru Europa”, a subliniat Zelenski.
